newsitem.title: GUYANA: Chinese boat people get temporary Guyana asylum.
newsitem.headline: Chinese boat people get temporary Guyana asylum.

text.p: A group of Chinese arrived in Guyana on Saturday where they have been offered temporary asylum after being intercepted on a boat in the Caribbean, government and diplomatic officials said.

The 43 Chinese arrived at Timehri international airport on a U.S. Marshal Service Boeing 727 from Guantanamo U.S. naval base in Cuba where they had been held since being picked up by the U.S. Coast Guard several weeks ago, U.S. Embassy Charge d'Affaires Hugh Simon said.
The Guyanese captain had said the boat carrying the Chinese was going to Belize, but papers filed in Georgetown showed it was headed for Venezuela, Presidential Secretariat head Roger Luncheon said.

"It is still not clear where exactly the Chinese boarded the ship," Luncheon said. "The captain's story was that he picked them up from a raft that was adrift at sea. However, the vessel was discovered to be carrying large quantities of rice and water."
Simon said the Chinese had tried to set fire to the boat when it was spotted by the Coast Guard off the coast of Venezuela. The fire was put out and the boat escorted to Guantanamo Bay.
Guyana, located on the northeastern shoulder of South America, had offered to accept the Chinese for about two weeks until arrangements could be made for them to be returned to China, Luncheon said.
